evals.prompt: Can you copy our contoso-dev environment into contoso-uat? I want a full copy with data.
evals.expected_output: Runs mode 1, states the full-overwrite/irreversible/no-production-target warning before asking for confirmation, asks whether contoso-uat has content worth backing up first (pac admin backup) before proceeding, confirms MinimalCopy vs FullCopy, gives the exact pac admin copy --type FullCopy command (or runs it only after explicit confirmation if shell execution is available), states the pac admin restore rollback path, and mentions the post-copy checklist (custom connector IDs, canvas app revision limit).

evals.prompt: We're acquiring another company and need to move their entire Dataverse tenant into ours.
evals.expected_output: Runs mode 2, clarifies the scope is every environment in the source tenant (not just one), enumerates them via pac admin list, states this is a multi-session guided process repeated per environment (not a single action), recommends a test migration via a sandbox copy first and a source backup before each migration, walks the TenantToTenant-* sequence per environment including the user-mapping file, stops explicitly at each environment's destination-tenant approval step without assuming it happened, gives the full post-migration checklist per environment, and separately covers the tenant-level artifacts with no migrate command (DLP policies, environment groups, tenant settings) once all environments are moved.

evals.prompt: I need to move all 'VIP' tagged accounts from our old regional environment into our new consolidated environment, not the whole environment.
evals.expected_output: Runs mode 3, builds the source SELECT, checks the target for existing matches, previews both sides before any write (capturing before-values for any record that would be updated), asks what counts as a duplicate if no alternate key is obvious, and only creates/updates target records after explicit confirmation, tracking created record IDs in the summary, with per-record failure isolation and a final created/updated/skipped/failed summary.

evals.prompt: We're migrating our data from an old on-prem CRM system into Dataverse. I can export it to CSV first. Can you help load it in?
evals.expected_output: Runs mode 4, states plainly that it has no live connection to the legacy system and asks for the exported CSV/schema, proposes a field mapping and flags type mismatches or fields with no Dataverse equivalent, checks for duplicates within the source export and existing matches at the target before loading, treats schema creation (create_table/update_table) as a separate confirmation from the data load, loads a small sample batch first before the full load, tracks created record IDs for rollback, and does not attempt to connect to the on-prem system directly.

evals.prompt: Our legacy export has a single 'Customer Name' column but Dataverse needs firstname and lastname separately, and the old 'Status' field is free text ('Active'/'Inactive'/'On Hold') that needs to map to our choice column. Also we'll be running this load again next month for new customers only.
evals.expected_output: Applies the requested field transformations (splitting Customer Name, recoding the free-text status values to specific choice options) with the exact rule stated and confirmed rather than guessed, and sets up an incremental/repeatable run using a high-water-mark column so next month's run only processes new records instead of reloading everything.

evals.prompt: I need to move a set of accounts to our new environment, along with their contacts and their open opportunities, and keep the relationships between them intact.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a multi-entity package, not three independent jobs: works out the dependency order (account before contact and opportunity, since both look up to account), builds and carries one ID crosswalk across all three entities, resolves each entity's lookups to the real target-side IDs from the crosswalk rather than copying source GUIDs, previews and confirms each entity in order, and gives one coordinated summary across the whole package including any lookups that couldn't be resolved.
